transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

This pattern usually means the dryer is overheating, triggering a safety cut-out to protect itself, then restarting once it cools down. The most common cause is restricted airflow from blocked filters or vents. Please check the fluff filter in the door opening and, if your model has one, the condenser unit at the bottom front. Are they completely clear of lint and debris?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
filter gets cleaned every time. no condenser its vented. the cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho

Since the filter is clean but the cabinet gets very hot before it cuts out, the heat isn't being carried away by the airflow. This suggests a blockage in the vent hose or at the external wall outlet, which traps the hot air inside and triggers the safety cut-out. Please check the flexible hose at the back of the dryer for kinks or lint buildup, and verify that the vent flap outside is opening properly when the machine runs. If the path is clear but it still overheats, we may need to check if the internal fan is working correctly.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
just looked, the hose is crushed behind the dryer where i pushed it back, and theres fluff in the folds of it

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That explains it perfectly. The crushed hose and the fluff trapped inside are blocking the air escape path, which causes the drum temperature to spike rapidly. This triggers the thermal safety cut-out you're seeing after 10 minutes. Please pull the dryer away from the wall again, straighten out the kinked section of the hose, and clear all the lint from the folds. If possible, detach the hose fully and blow through it or use a vacuum to ensure there is no further blockage inside the ducting. If it still cuts out after clearing the hose, the issue may be deeper inside the machine (such as a blocked blower fan housing), in which case we would need to look at internal components or call an engineer.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will do that. its my landlords dryer tho, do i need to tell him? model on the door label says IDV 75 if u need it

Yes, you must tell your landlord. This is a fire risk because the trapped lint and heat can ignite if not cleared properly. Please straighten the hose fully and clear all the fluff from inside it before using the machine again. If it still cuts out after you have fixed the hose, there may be an internal blockage or fan fault that requires a professional engineer.
